transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that my head just feels really cloudy lately. I manage some properties, and I'll find myself just staring at a board packet or an email from a vendor... and I just can't decide on anything. Even simple things that I used to handle real fast, I just can't seem to figure out right now.
Beyond this difficulty with decision-making, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I just... I really haven't wanted to do much of anything lately. Like, I haven't wanted to go to my dance class, or even just go look at the little galleries like I normally do. I haven't even felt like cooking Sunday food for my family. And, well, those are the things that usually make me feel like myself. I just don't have the interest right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been going on for about two weeks. I just noticed this... sharper change in my energy and my confidence, and then this low, cloudy feeling set in. It all really started right around the time my husband retired and was suddenly home all day.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. I mean, I still go to bed and wake up around the same times I usually do. My sleep has been pretty normal, honestly, it's just during the day that I feel so down.
Given how you've been feeling, how much difficulty are you having with your daily responsibilities, such as managing your properties or interacting with your family?

I'm still getting to work every day, I make sure of that. But... it is harder. I've had to slow down a lot on making decisions. I'm actually having my assistant double-check all the vendor details for the properties right now, just to be safe. And I've even had to put off a couple of items for the board. I just... I really don't trust my own judgment at the moment.
How much of your day is spent feeling this way, and do these feelings make it significantly difficult for you to function at work or at home?

Well, it's pretty much most of the day. From the time I get up until I go to bed, that cloudy, heavy feeling is just sort of sitting there. As for functioning... I wouldn't say it's impossible, but it is definitely a struggle. Like I mentioned, I'm still going to work and getting things done, but I'm having to lean a lot more on my assistant and put things off because I just don't feel sharp. At home, with my husband being around all the time now, it's just... I'm getting through the day, but it takes a lot more effort than it used to.
Are you able to continue with your usual social and work activities, or have you had to significantly reduce or stop them because of how you are feeling?

I haven't stopped anything completely, no. Like I said, I'm still going in to work and doing what I need to do. I haven't really reduced my hours or anything like that. I'm just... taking it slower. I haven't backed out of any social things either, mostly because my husband and I don't do a whole lot of that anyway. So, no, I'm still doing my usual activities, it's just harder to get through them.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or your weight since these feelings began?

My eating has definitely been a little off lately. I just don't have much of an appetite during the day. I usually just have some coffee and maybe a couple bites of something, and that carries me through most of the afternoon. Then at night, I just kind of pick at things... maybe some tortillas or some sweets, but I'm not really enjoying it. I'm just eating because I know I should. I haven't really noticed a big change in my weight, though, just the appetite.
When you are at work or with your family, do you find that your symptoms cause you significant distress, or is the main issue just that tasks feel more effortful to complete?

I wouldn't call it significant distress, no. It's really just that everything takes more effort and I'm second-guessing myself a lot. I am still getting to work every day, but I've had to slow down on making decisions. I've been asking my assistant to double-check all the vendor details for me, and I even had to put off a couple of board items recently. I just really don't trust my own judgment right now. So, it's mostly just the struggle of getting the work done right, rather than feeling distressed about it.
